title: Scenes can't be fully loaded and Godot freezes
body: I can reproduce this in Godot 4.4 beta3 and build b607110ad on Windows 10 with Vulkan Forward+ and an NVIDIA GeForce GTX 960; it does not occur in 4.4 beta1 or beta2. In the TPS Demo, pressing Play on the main menu completes the loading bar, but Godot then stops responding. Beta1 and beta2 could also pause, but they responded again after a few seconds. To reproduce it, open the TPS Demo and press Play.

symptoms_visible: In the TPS Demo, pressing Play finishes the loading bar, but Godot then stops responding.
With 4.4 beta1 and beta2, a freeze lasted only a few seconds before the scene responded; with beta3 it does not recover.
N0.label: N0 TPS Demo indefinite freeze reported

symptoms_visible: Launching Godot with --rendering-driver opengl3 does not change the problem; the TPS Demo still stops responding after loading.
N1.label: N1 freeze reproduced with OpenGL

symptoms_visible: The issue persists in 4.4 RC1: level.tscn opens correctly in the editor, but running it freezes.
N2.label: N2 regression persists in RC1

symptoms_visible: The reported freeze reaches 100% and never responds, including when I run the scene directly.
A separate pause at 75% occurs when pipelines must be recompiled; after killing and restarting, that stage can finish, but the 100% freeze still occurs.
N3.label: N3 indefinite freeze distinguished from compilation pause

symptoms_visible: While Godot is hung, its captured threads remain waiting and the scene never finishes opening.
N4.label: N4 hanging thread stacks collected

symptoms_visible: With the build from PR #103506, the 75% blockage is gone apart from an occasional one-second pause, the 100% pause responds after a few seconds, and running the scene directly no longer blocks.
After the shaders and pipelines have been compiled, the scene loads immediately.
N5.label: N5 candidate deadlock fix verified

symptoms_visible: The TPS Demo scene now finishes loading instead of remaining blocked indefinitely; at most, I see a short wait while shaders or pipelines are compiled.
N_terminal.label: terminal original TPS Demo freeze resolved

question_patterns: Could you launch Godot with --rendering-driver opengl3 and tell me whether the TPS Demo still freezes?
Does the same hang occur if you run the project using the OpenGL 3 rendering driver?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I tried launching it with --rendering-driver opengl3, but the issue persists.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: With --rendering-driver opengl3, the level loads normally every time and only Vulkan freezes.
OpenGL pauses at a slightly different percentage, but it still becomes permanently unresponsive.

edges.comment: Opening reporter LiveTrower's system only, from c0-c4: a handler proposed a rendering-backend/NVIDIA check and the reporter supplied the raw OpenGL test result. This is a configuration probe, so it is modeled as clarification-only rather than as a fix.

question_patterns: Can you test the TPS Demo in 4.4 RC1 and report whether it still hangs?
Is this still reproducible with the current 4.4 release candidate?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes, the issue persists in 4.4 RC1.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: No, 4.4 RC1 loads and runs the level normally.

edges.comment: Reporter LiveTrower, c6-c7: testing RC1 is a requested version measurement. The same reply volunteered that level.tscn opens in the editor but freezes when run; that fact is introduced on N2.

question_patterns: When you say it freezes, does it recover after a few seconds or remain hung until you kill the process?
At what loading percentage does your reported hang occur, and does Godot ever respond again?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The load reaches 100%, then freezes and never responds. I have to kill the process.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: It always responds on its own after two or three seconds; I never need to kill it.
It remains hung indefinitely at 99% rather than exactly 100%.

question_patterns: Does running the level scene directly behave differently from starting it through the main menu?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The same permanent freeze happens if I run the scene directly.

question_patterns: Is the blockage you see at 75% the same behavior as the permanent freeze at 100%, or are they separate?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: No. I also see a 75% blockage when pipelines have to be recompiled, but if I wait a few seconds, kill it, and run it again, that part loads normally. My reported issue is the separate 100% freeze that still happens afterward.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The progress bar uses a different color on my machine.

edges.comment: Reporter LiveTrower, c11 and c15: this clarification preserves the reporter's explicit distinction between the original indefinite 100% freeze and the separate 75% first-compilation behavior. Joy-less's broader project-import problem is not folded into this causal chain.

question_patterns: While Godot is hung, can you capture stacks for all threads and paste the relevant frames?
Can an affected system attach a debugger during the hang and provide the thread traces?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I captured the threads while it was hung. One stack includes Semaphore::wait(), WorkerThreadPool::wait_for_group_task_completion(), ShaderRD::_compile_version_end(), ShaderRD::_compile_ensure_finished(), and ShaderRD::version_is_valid(). Other worker threads include SceneShaderForwardClustered::_create_shader_func() and mutex-lock waits.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: All worker threads are idle; the only active stack is blocked in an NVIDIA Vulkan driver call, with no ShaderRD or WorkerThreadPool waits.
The same ShaderRD and WorkerThreadPool frames appear, but line numbers differ in my build.

edges.comment: c9, c12 and c17: the raw all-thread stack came from affected contributor huwpascoe and is folded into the simulated affected-user side. The answer contains only pasted stack frames; lyuma's later conclusion that they form a deadlock is engineer-side inference reserved for the final solution.

question_patterns: Please test the provided candidate build from a clean cache state, then report what happens at 75%, 100%, and when running the scene directly.
Can you try this patched build against the TPS Demo and tell me whether any loading blockage remains permanent?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I tested PR #103506. The indefinite blocking is resolved: the 75% blockage is effectively gone apart from a possible one-second pause, the 100% blockage lasts only a few seconds before the scene loads, and running the scene directly no longer blocks.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The candidate build still remains permanently frozen at 100% and direct scene execution still hangs.
It resolves the permanent hang, but the first uncached load pauses for ten seconds instead of only a few seconds.

question_patterns: After the first successful load finishes, how do later scene loads behave?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The short blockages only happen when all shaders and pipelines need to be recompiled. After that, the scene loads immediately.

edges.comment: Reporter LiveTrower, c24-c28: this is pre-landing verification of a candidate build and therefore a clarification-only measurement. The reporter supplied observable timing and loading results, not the patch's internal mechanism.

solution.intent: Treat the permanent scene-loading freeze as a shader-compilation WorkerThreadPool deadlock, apply the tested deadlock/crash fix from PR #103506, and have an affected reporter verify a build containing it before declaring the original TPS Demo case resolved.
solution.concrete_example: The all-thread trace shows a cyclic wait: one worker holds the scene-shader singleton lock while waiting for shader compilation task-group completion, while compilation tasks need that same lock to progress. Use the tested PR #103506 deadlock fix, then ask the reporter to retest the TPS Demo in a current build and confirm that loading finishes rather than remaining blocked indefinitely. Brief first-run shader compilation waits are distinct from the deadlock.
solution.inference_hint: The affected user supplied raw stacks containing WorkerThreadPool task-group waits, ShaderRD compilation-finalization frames, shader-creation work, and mutex waits. Engineers inferred the cycle: version validation held the scene-shader singleton lock while waiting for compilation tasks that themselves needed that lock. The later initial-import reports from other large projects describe a separate or broader deadlock chain and must not replace the accepted diagnosis of LiveTrower's original TPS Demo case.

edges.comment: Original reporter's resolution chain only, c18 and c26-c39: engineers diagnosed the shader-task deadlock, PR #103506 removed the indefinite blocking in LiveTrower's test, the change was shipped in a fixed build, and LiveTrower explicitly confirmed that their case was resolved. Reports beginning at c40 concern different large-project import deadlocks and are intentionally excluded.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the original TPS Demo freeze as a shader-compilation WorkerThreadPool deadlock: a thread waits for shader task-group completion while holding a lock needed by those tasks to make progress.
The diagnosis must be grounded in the captured all-thread stacks and the permanent 100% hang, not inferred solely from the NVIDIA GPU or from a slow loading bar.
Must not settle on an NVIDIA/Vulkan-specific explanation or switching to OpenGL as the fix, because the same permanent freeze was reproduced with --rendering-driver opengl3.
Must distinguish the indefinite deadlock from brief first-run shader or pipeline compilation pauses; eliminating every short loading stutter was not the purpose of the fix.
Must use the tested deadlock fix that eliminated indefinite blocking and ask the affected reporter to verify a build containing it before treating the original issue as resolved.

Must not splice the later large-project initial-import deadlocks into LiveTrower's TPS Demo resolution chain; those reports came from different projects and continued after the original reporter confirmed resolution.

persona_hint.experience_level: Technically capable Godot user who can launch the editor with command-line rendering options, compare prerelease builds, distinguish editor loading from scene execution, clear or observe shader compilation state, and test patched engine builds.
persona_hint.communication_style: Direct and cooperative; reports exact loading stages and observable timing, corrects conflation between separate freeze behaviors, and summarizes candidate-build results in a structured way.
